target.title: fix(cli): clarify nodes invoke params errors
target.body:
﻿Closes #101835

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw nodes invoke --params <bad-json>` would see a raw JSON parse failure when the `--params` option was malformed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `nodes invoke` command now validates its local command inputs before resolving the node through the gateway, and wraps malformed `--params` JSON with an option-specific CLI error. The fix stays inside the existing nodes CLI command boundary and does not change gateway payload behavior for valid JSON.

## User Impact

Users now get an actionable `--params must be valid JSON.` error, and malformed local input does not open a gateway call before failing.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Current head `99ef69303cf39b052e2ad5ffad107489e8f0df81` rejects malformed `nodes invoke --params` at the nodes CLI command boundary before resolving a node or opening a gateway call.
- Command-boundary proof for the requested CLI action, using the same `nodes invoke --node mac-1 --command canvas.eval --params not-json` argv against `src/cli/nodes-cli/register.invoke.ts`:
  ```text
  cmd /v:on /c "node --import tsx --input-type=module -e ""import { Command } from 'commander'; import { registerNodesInvokeCommands } from './src/cli/nodes-cli/register.invoke.ts'; const nodes = new Command('nodes'); nodes.exitOverride(); registerNodesInvokeCommands(nodes); await nodes.parseAsync(['invoke','--node','mac-1','--command','canvas.eval','--params','not-json'], { from: 'user' });"" 2>&1 & echo __EXIT_CODE__=!ERRORLEVEL!"
  nodes invoke failed: --params must be valid JSON.
  __EXIT_CODE__=1
  ```
- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/nodes-cli.coverage.test.ts` passed (`1` file, `23` tests).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub current-head checks: `gh pr checks 101838 --repo openclaw/openclaw --json name,bucket,state,completedAt,link` showed no failed buckets; current checks are pass/skip/neutral.
- Duplicate search before issue creation: open issue/PR searches for `nodes invoke params JSON` and `malformed --params nodes invoke` returned no blockers.

Observed result: malformed `--params` now reports `--params must be valid JSON.`; the focused regression also asserts no gateway call and no `node.invoke` call are made.

target.title: feat(channels): expose source actor attribution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel context tests cover generic `SourceActor` projection and object-to-scalar mirror parity.
- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.
- Signal mention-gating tests cover Signal sender identity mapping into the generic context.
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `SourceActor*` parity with production inbound context.
- Focused tests passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK API check passed without a baseline hash diff:
  `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Redacted Runtime Proof

Temporary local proof harness imported production `buildChannelInboundEventContext` and printed the emitted prompt context on PR head `5fab61f873`. The proof preserves the emitted source-actor shape while replacing all Signal identifiers, group identifiers, participant names, phone numbers, UUIDs, and message bodies with placeholders.

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<redacted proof harness>'
runtime-proof:environment
{
  "pr": 96863,
  "repo": "openclaw/openclaw",
  "head": "5fab61f873",
  "node": "v26.3.0"
}
runtime-proof:#96863 source actor fields emitted by prompt context
{
  "SourceActor": {
    "id": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
    "peerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
    "displayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
    "role": "participant",
    "context": "signal-group:<redacted>"
  },
  "SourceActorId": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
  "SourceActorPeerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
  "SourceActorDisplayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
  "SourceActorRole": "participant",
  "SourceActorContext": "signal-group:<redacted>",
  "scalarMirrorMatches": {
    "id": true,
    "peerId": true,
    "displayName": true,
    "role": true,
    "context": true
  }
}
```

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

A private Signal group smoke was run after a production config hotfix that kept the group-bound agent responding without changing Docker permissions. The private runtime intentionally stayed on its deployed OpenClaw release instead of being advanced to this PR stack today; the facts below are operational evidence for the real Signal group route, not an additional claim that this PR head is live-deployed.

Sanitized facts:

- `openclaw config validate` against `/run/user/1000/openclaw/openclaw.json`: `valid=true`, exit `0`.
- `openclaw-gateway.service`: `active/running`, `NRestarts=0`.
- A native Signal mention from a group participant produced an outbound group reply; the journal recorded `delivered reply to group` at `2026-06-26T13:03:19+02:00`.
- Latest group-bound Signal session metadata for the private family agent: `systemSent=true`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
- Journal after the smoke: `Failed to inspect sandbox image` count `0`.

Deployment note: the private runtime is not being upgraded to this stack today because that would mix the PR validation with an unrelated Docker sandbox repair. The long-term Docker/rootless sandbox fix is being tracked separately.
## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Evidence update

Current-head proof on `codex/source-actor-context-contract` (`4647951f5b`):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 28.32s

$ node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check
OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256

$ git diff --check
# passed with no output
```

GitHub state after the current-head push:

- `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`
- `Real behavior proof=SUCCESS`
- `git diff --check` clean locally before push

Inspectable assertions covered:

- `SourceActor` is the canonical attribution object.
- `SourceActorId`, `SourceActorPeerId`, `SourceActorDisplayName`,
  `SourceActorRole`, and `SourceActorContext` mirror the canonical object.
- The plugin SDK runtime mock now mirrors both the canonical object and the scalar fields.
- The stack inherits #96862's `WasMentioned` compatibility fix: delivered Signal turns
  keep `WasMentioned` as the effective mention-gating result.
- The stack inherits #96862's canonical mention-policy shape: `GroupRequireMention`,
  not a duplicate `RequireMention` alias.
- The plugin SDK runtime mock mirrors `MentionShouldSkip`.
- `SourceActor.role` is constrained to the typed role set:
  `operator`, `participant`, `self`, `system`, `external`.
- Type docs state that display names and peer ids are channel-supplied metadata,
  not trusted authorization facts.

No private Signal identifiers, phone numbers, participant names, or group ids are used in this proof.
